edge-ai: A cutaway illustration of several real-world devices operating at the network’s edge: a roadside security camera, a warehouse robot arm, and a moving vehicle, each receiving streams from its own camera, radar, or other sensors into a small glowing AI chip inside the device; beside each chip, tiny visual labels suggest constrained battery power, heat, memory, and processor capacity, while a distant cloud data centre is shown across a broken or weak network connection with most raw data remaining local. The camera’s model draws a box around a person, the robot’s model outlines a parcel before the arm reaches for it, and the vehicle’s model highlights an obstacle from fused sensor views, but in each case the output travels to a clearly separate human supervisor or conventional control panel that makes or authorizes the next action, emphasizing that local AI recognition can be fast, private, bandwidth-saving, and resilient offline without necessarily being autonomous.
machine-vision: A clear cutaway-style illustration of a factory-and-street scene viewed through several machine-vision cameras: on the left, a fixed camera above a conveyor identifies, measures and rejects a missing or misaligned part with simple geometric overlays; in the center, a neural-network vision module receives many varied training images—sun, rain, night, different vehicles and objects—before sending labeled outputs to a robot arm and a dashboard where a human checks results; on the right, a vehicle camera tries to recognize road lanes, buildings and pedestrians as weather shifts from bright sun to fog and rain, with some labels becoming uncertain or wrong when an object is shadowed, covered, or altered with camouflage. Show the full system chain—lens, image data, software model, confidence indicator, and physical machine action—while a small inset contrasts a computer chip merely sitting inside a device with a connected, validated vision system authorized to control it.
terminal-guidance: A clear cutaway infographic-style illustration showing a missile in the final seconds of flight descending toward a target area, with its earlier route behind it marked by a dashed line labeled “coordinates / satellite navigation / inertial guidance,” while its nose-mounted seeker scans ahead through several translucent wedges representing radar, infrared heat, laser reflection, and camera vision; inside the missile, a small computer combines sensor data and estimated position into steering commands that visibly move the control fins toward a highlighted aim point. Below, split the target area into two contrasting panels: on one side, a human operator identifies and designates a specific target before the weapon homes in; on the other, an automated visual system searches among several similar vehicles or objects and places a tracking box around one, with a prominent question mark between “tracking a selected target” and “selecting a target,” making the difference between technical guidance and authority to choose unmistakable.
